messages:
helen: Hey team — Saturn Health POC kickoff. We're showing the SampleApp using the modular SDK with streaming + tool/function calls and structured JSON outputs. Quick asks: handshake steps for the SDK (ephemeral creds), recommended stream settings for backpressure, and a short pricing ballpark for a sustained 40 req/s workload (~1k tokens avg resp). Can someone drop a tiny runbook/snippet I can share with the customer? :wave:
mike: Quick Q — hosted or dedicated for the POC? That changes the creds/workflow.
helen: Hosted to start. They may want Dedicated later if latency/SLAs look good. For now need hosted runbook only.
raj: OK — for hosted POC here's the short checklist I usually share: 1) mint ephemeral creds via presales token service; 2) init SDK with the ephemeral token; 3) open streaming connection w/ subprotocol `rwd-stream-v1`; 4) send initial meta frame with schema id; 5) stream chat/inputs; 6) respond to `toolcall` events with `tool_response` frames.
amy: For structured outputs we recommend including the JSON Schema in the initial meta so the runtime validates/flags regressions. We also add an eval hook to assert key fields.
raj: Snippet for the SDK (very minimal):
```js
// init with ephemeral token (node)
const client = new RedwoodClient({ token: EPHEMERAL_TOKEN, streaming: true, multiplex: true });
const stream = await client.stream({ model: 'rwd-4-small', input: prompt });
stream.on('chunk', (c) => { /* aggregate tokens, look for toolcall */ });
stream.on('toolcall', async (tc) => {
  // call external booking API then send tool_response frame
  const result = await callBooking(tc.args);
  stream.send({ type: 'tool_response', id: tc.id, result });
});
```
helen: Nice. For handshake — what's the minimal HTTP flow I give them?
raj: Minimal handshake example: POST /v1/handshake with service API key -> returns ephemeral token + expires_in. Then client uses that token in `Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>` for socket open. If a 401 happens SDK will call the refresh callback if you provide `credentialProvider`. Example meta frame on connect: `{ type: 'meta', schema_id: 'saturn-v1', client_version: 'sampleapp-0.3' }`.
mike: Pricing ballpark for hosted steady load: rough estimate — expect hosted inference spend to be the dominant line. For 40 rps @ ~1k tokens / response that's ~144M tokens/day. Ballpark cost could be low thousands/month; I'll pull actual pricing numbers and get back to you.
amy: Also call out tokenization variance — if their prompts are long the token count jumps. Recommend a quick demo run with representative inputs to get close estimate.
helen: Can you paste a copy-paste runbook I can drop into their doc? One-liner steps + sample curl.
raj: Pasteable runbook: 
1) Presales: call `POST https://internal.presales.redwood/api/ephemeral` with your account id -> returns `{ token, expires_in }`.
2) Init SDK w/ token: `const c = new RedwoodClient({ token })`.
3) Open stream: WebSocket `wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1?model=rwd-4-small` using header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and subprotocol `rwd-stream-v1`.
4) Send meta frame: {"type":"meta","schema_id":"saturn-v1"}.
5) Production of structured outputs: include `schema` in request or `meta.schema_id`. SDK will surface `toolcall` frames. Reply with `tool_response` frames.
6) If you need higher throughput for the POC, switch to batch requests or request a short Dedicated trial.
Example curl for handshake (presales dev env):
```bash
curl -X POST https://internal.presales.redwood/api/ephemeral -H 'Authorization: Bearer PRESALES_KEY' -d '{"account":"saturn-health"}'
```
helen: Perfect — I'll paste that into the customer doc.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: sampleapp/presales-runbooks v1.2 — 2 files updated :rocket:
mike: I'll follow up on firm pricing numbers and a note about limits/quotas. Also confirm we can enable short Dedicated trial if they ask.
helen: Thanks all — sending to customer now and booking a 30m demo for Fri. If anything else pops up I'll ping here. :thumbsup:
